clue.text: I would return to position in space

indicators.note: return asks for the abbreviation of the opening words to be read backwards

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd, giving ID
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to go back to their post somewhere out in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' applies only to the contraction I'd, turning it round before the posture word is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Space and distance are both the gap or interval separating two points.

clue.text: Take away, from French channel

parts.note: de is French for from
a duct is a channel or pipe

explanation.surface: Subtract something, coming from a French TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests TV, but here it is a conduit.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct is to subtract an amount from a total.

clue.text: Agricultural implement to mark, if that is right

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
taken as written
ie abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A farm tool used to make marks, provided that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarifier is a harrow-like machine that breaks up topsoil or rakes out moss.

clue.text: Where, in the world, NEWS comes from

definitions.text: Where, in the world, NEWS comes from

parts.words: Where, in the world, NEWS comes from
parts.note: NEWS is read as the initials of the compass points North, East, West, South, so it comes from every direction

explanation.surface: Asking where on earth the news originates.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals give the game away: N, E, W and S are the four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from every direction, the four points of the compass.

clue.text: Type of soap from former Spanish kingdom.

explanation.surface: A brand of soap named after an old Iberian realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild olive-oil soap is named after the central Spanish region, once an independent kingdom.

clue.text: Young scout embracing her could be a sweet child

indicators.note: embracing means the scout's letters wrap around the following word

parts.note: a Cub is a junior member of the Scout movement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Cub Scout giving a girl a hug might seem an adorable youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young scout' is one idea, a junior in the Scout movement, and 'could be' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged infant angel in art, hence any angelic, lovable little one.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon rebel was in this place to protect the ceremonial vigil

parts.note: here means in this place
to ward is to guard or protect
taken as written
a wake is a watch kept over a body before burial

explanation.surface: An old English rebel stood here guarding a funeral watch.
explanation.definitionFit: This eleventh-century Englishman led resistance to the Norman conquest from the Fens.

clue.text: Prevail in wet weather we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for wet weather is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Hold sway in a downpour, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule or hold sway, so to prevail.

clue.text: Slaughter, however dear, in France, is on your head

parts.note: but means however
cher is French for dear

indicators.note: your head is the first letter of the word your

explanation.surface: Bloodshed, but, dear, in France it is on your own head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on' is a link; 'your head' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchery is wholesale, brutal killing.

clue.text: Right Excellent man could be a ruler

parts.note: E is a grade letter for excellent
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A thoroughly upright gentleman would make a good governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent governs on behalf of a monarch who is too young or absent.

clue.text: Drag to the left and speak slowly

parts.note: to draw is to pull or drag along

explanation.surface: An instruction to pull something leftwards and talk unhurriedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to talk with slow, drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: Pierce coin, it should add flavour

parts.note: to spear is to pierce with a point
to mint is to coin money

explanation.surface: Stabbing a coin, oddly, is supposed to improve the taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a herb whose oil is used to give gum, sweets and toothpaste their taste.

clue.text: Creditor in old merchandise producing old female dress

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor
taken as written
a line is a range of goods a shop stocks

explanation.surface: A lender dealing in old stock comes up with an antique frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinoline was a stiffened hooped petticoat worn under Victorian skirts.

clue.text: Pull to be first in front of church

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: to win is to come first in a race

explanation.surface: An urge to pull ahead and arrive first outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To winch is to haul something up with a windlass or cable drum.

clue.text: Recipe concocted by former American president

indicators.note: concocted means the letters of recipe are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe dreamed up by an ex-president of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin Pierce was the fourteenth US head of state, in office 1853 to 1857.

clue.text: Part-time soldier making survey of land

explanation.surface: A reservist moonlighting as a land surveyor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a member of the part-time Territorial Army is a Territorial, informally a 'terrier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Territorial Army volunteer is nicknamed this, and a terrier is also a register or survey of an estate's landholdings.

clue.text: Victim, even without medicine, could produce a violent utterance

indicators.note: could produce says the letters left over may be rearranged into something new
without means a letter is taken away from the word victim

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for medicine, as in a medical degree

explanation.surface: A victim deprived of drugs might well let rip with abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes M from VICTIM, leaving VICTI; 'could produce' rearranges VICTI with EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Invective is abusive, vehement language.

clue.text: Feigned to be deeply moved

explanation.surface: Putting it on, or really overcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected means pretended or artificial, and also emotionally touched.

clue.text: Good Luck concerning melody

parts.note: for can mean concerning or regarding
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Wishing someone well about a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune means chance, especially chance that turns out well.

clue.text: Assemble material partly as a symbol

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Put together some fabric to form a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a device or badge that stands for something.

clue.text: Putting it back in part of church could be intrinsic

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the church section

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: back means the little word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: Restoring something to its place in a church might be thought essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI, which goes 'in' NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Native qualities are inborn or inherent ones, belonging by nature.

clue.text: Normal and ordinary, but certainly not sharp

explanation.surface: A plain, everyday person who is no quick wit.
explanation.walkthrough: In music a natural is a note neither sharp nor flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means usual or unaffected, and in music a note that is neither raised nor lowered.

clue.text: Type of cord found in the back

explanation.surface: A kind of string located behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The nerve bundle in the backbone is the spinal cord, and the adjective means relating to the backbone.

clue.text: Enigmatic composer of large arrangements

indicators.note: arrangements suggests the musical reworking of the word large into another order

explanation.surface: A mysterious composer known for big orchestral arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangements' rearranges LARGE. The definition alludes to Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar wrote the Enigma Variations, so the adjective points to him.

clue.text: Travel right to the south-east for a shrub

parts.note: to go is to travel
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Head right towards the south-east in search of a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered bush of heaths, also called furze.

clue.text: Flatter container for a flower

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them
a cup is a container for drink

explanation.surface: Sweet-talk a vessel into holding a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like an adjective (more level) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow meadow plant in bloom in early summer.

clue.text: Soldier with a shield making sailor get Early English right

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shield-bearing infantryman persuading a seaman to obtain early English rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A targeteer was a foot soldier armed with a targe, a small round buckler.

clue.text: A line that could be foreign

indicators.note: could be says the letters of a line might form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A single line of text that might come from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means strange, belonging to another country or place.

clue.text: Over-elegant garment before this year?

indicators.note: before puts the garment ahead of the letter for year

parts.note: a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a frock is a touch too smart for this season.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are showy or overly smart for the occasion.

clue.text: Dancing girl holding wild hyacinth

explanation.surface: A dancer clutching a woodland flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bluebell Girls are a famous troupe of dancers at the Lido in Paris; 'holding' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Paris Lido dance troupe bears this name, and the plant is the wild hyacinth of British woods.
